- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or mean reversion.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in the 10–15 day horizon after spikes; apply downward correction for short-term momentum.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-stage mean reversion; add a 2–3% downward bias if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast decline.
- Avoid over-relying on recent high sentiment to justify long-term forecasts; use 3–5 day moving average of sentiment to temper overconfidence.
